name: Activity
summary: Present caller-owned task statuses as dense rows with aggregate and item disclosures.

useWhen: Present caller-owned task statuses as dense rows with aggregate and item disclosures.
avoidWhen: Executing remote tasks, managing backend state or simulating assistant processing.

obligations: Action records use id/label/onAction/disabled and perform only their supplied callbacks. Details and action controls remain outside summary. Visible words and decorative marks distinguish every state beyond color.
A polite atomic region announces aggregate label/status independently of elapsed time, metadata and details. Native button and summary controls keep visible focus and forced-color semantics.

behavior: The native div attributes/ref/events retain their meanings. label names the aggregate; items have unique nonempty stable IDs, label and queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled status. Optional details, context, meta, caller time and action records remain caller-owned content.

An omitted aggregate status follows failed, running, queued, cancelled, then completed priority across nonempty items. Empty items have a neutral No activity state unless an explicit status is supplied. There are no cosmetic timers, task execution, requests or simulated processing.

expanded/onExpandedChange or defaultExpanded control aggregate disclosure. Rows with details/context/actions use native details/summary keyboard disclosure; rows without details have no dead disclosure control.

Aggregate and native item disclosures reuse DisclosureGroup's finite height, opacity and chevron motion. System or explicit reduced motion settles immediately; collapsing content leaves focus and accessibility navigation before its visual exit completes.

Action records use id/label/onAction/disabled and perform only their supplied callbacks. Details and action controls remain outside summary. Visible words and decorative marks distinguish every state beyond color.
A polite atomic region announces aggregate label/status independently of elapsed time, metadata and details. Native button and summary controls keep visible focus and forced-color semantics.
accessibility: Preserve native host/ref/events and keyboard controls with visible focus.
Use semantic labels and static status announcements; do not rely on color or continuously animated processing.

requirements.reason: Native dynamic colors do not apply to the React web binding.
Native font metrics do not apply to the React web binding.
